This is not good, we are using `useEffect` here as an escape hatch. Also, because we are using `useEffect`, this happens after browser already painted, it would cause UI thrashing: for one frame we would show some Fiber selected, while results are empty.

We should do these state updates directly in a render function. More info here - https://react.dev/learn/you-might-not-need-an-effect#chains-of-computations.

Removed the effect and updated the selection during render using the same previous-value pattern already used for `prevProfilingData` in this file. This keeps the search results and selected item in sync within the same render, avoiding the brief post-paint frame where the selection could become stale. One thing to note is that renders can't dispatch to the Components tree, so keyboard search navigation no longer updates the selection there (mouse clicks still do). If that's important, I can add it back through a small dedicated sync path.

I don't think this is the same thing as an inline stylesheet. The `href` for an inline stylesheet is meant for deduping. `ReactDOM.preload` is for an actual resource.

The report is for a Flight issue so the test should showcase that scenario. The test should also use `hydrateRoot`. You'd never want to client-render over SSRed content.

There's no cascading update if it's within render. It's only cascading if it requires a rerender after commit (e.g. from within Effects). State updates during render are immediately applied and not considered cascading.
The original issue did not create the Promise in the state initializer which is fundamentally different. Creating new Promises in state initializers or `useMemo` is not supported.

This is not actually right. This was wrong for `Offscreen` too.

In the case of `const LazyActivity = React.lazy(async () => ({ default: React.Activity })); <LazyActivity />` the `elementType` should be the Lazy wrapper object. Otherwise reconciliation won't work correctly.

In fact, it looks like we get this wrong for all these built-ins so wrapping them would yield the wrong reconciliation.

So it's an existing bug that we need to fix separately.
